questions.stem: All paramedics are trained in emergency protocols. Some trained people are first-aiders. Which conclusion follows?

options.C: It is possible that some paramedics are first-aiders.

questions.stem: Which statement is logically equivalent to: 'You can submit the report only if your manager approves it'?

options.A: If your manager approves it, you can submit the report.
options.B: If you submit the report, your manager approved it.
options.C: If your manager does not approve it, you can submit the report.
options.D: If you do not submit the report, your manager did not approve it.

questions.stem: If today is Friday, what day will it be 365 days from today? (Assume a non‑leap year.)
Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability the sum is a prime number?
A jar has 8 red, 5 blue and 7 green beads. Two beads are drawn without replacement. What is the probability the two beads are different colours?
A bag contains 6 orange, 4 purple and 2 white tiles. One tile is drawn. What is P(orange | not white)?
Claim: 'Adding a second identity check before blood transfusion reduces wrong-patient errors.' Which evidence most strengthens the claim?

options.A: After the second check was introduced, wrong-patient errors fell compared with similar wards that did not introduce the change over the same period.
options.C: The hospital changed its uniform policy at the same time.
options.D: Some patients dislike being asked questions.

questions.stem: Claim: 'A new online booking system reduced missed appointments.' Which information most weakens the claim?

options.A: At the same time, the clinic started sending reminder texts to all patients.
options.D: The clinic repainted the waiting room.

questions.stem: Rule: If a shipment is international, delivery takes more than 7 days. A delivery took 5 days. What follows?

options.D: The shipment must be by air.

questions.stem: A box contains 3 defective and 17 non-defective items. Two items are selected without replacement. What is the probability at least one is defective?
A fair coin is flipped 7 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 3 heads?
A fair coin is flipped 6 times. What is the probability of getting at least 5 heads?
Four tasks (A, B, C, D) are scheduled Mon–Thu, one per day. Rules: B is on Tuesday. D is immediately after B. A is before C. Which day is C on?
Some architects are cyclists. No cyclists are scuba divers. Which statement must be true?

options.A: Some architects are not scuba divers.

questions.stem: A test has 90% sensitivity and 85% specificity. Prevalence is 10%. If a person tests positive, what is the approximate probability they truly have the condition?
A test has 90% sensitivity and 85% specificity. Prevalence is 10%. Approximately what percentage of people will test positive?
If the sample is contaminated, the culture will be invalid. The culture is valid. What follows?

options.C: The sample might or might not be contaminated.
options.D: The lab must repeat the culture.

questions.stem: Five books (H, I, J, K, L) are placed on a shelf. H is left of J. K is immediately right of I. L is not at either end. Which arrangement is possible?
A raffle ticket has a 0.03 chance of winning £80 and otherwise wins £0. What is the expected value?
A meeting starts at 14:18. It lasts 2 hours 47 minutes. What time does it end?
